title: Travel, problems & emergencies
goal: Handle hotels, trains and travel problems, report a loss or theft, get help in an emergency, and use 'if ... then' sentences.
intro:
Things go wrong when travelling: a missed train, a lost bag, a breakdown or a sudden illness. This unit gives you the words to explain the problem and ask for help, from a hotel desk to a police station.

The grammar is the **conditional**: Kannada makes 'if' with a single suffix, **-ಅರೆ**, attached to the past stem: ಬಂದರೆ 'if (someone) comes', ಮಳೆ ಬಂದರೆ 'if it rains'.

vocab.note: Spoken: ಅರ್ಜೆಂಟ್ arjeṇṭ. National emergency number: 112.
Police station: ಪೊಲೀಸ್ ಠಾಣೆ / ಪೊಲೀಸ್ ಸ್ಟೇಷನ್.

vocab.en: to be seen, appear; to see
vocab.note: Dative: ನನಗೆ ಕಾಣ್ತಿಲ್ಲ 'I can't see (it)'. Past ಕಂಡೆ.

vocab.en: to go bad, break down, spoil
vocab.note: ಕಾರು ಕೆಟ್ಟು ಹೋಯ್ತು 'the car broke down'.

phrases.en: I need to file a complaint.
Do you have a room available?
How much is it per night?
The AC in the room isn't working.
When's the next train to Mysuru?

phrases.native: ನನಗೆ ಕನ್ನಡ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಬರಲ್ಲ, ಇಂಗ್ಲಿಷ್ ಬರುತ್ತಾ?
phrases.roman: nanage kannaḍa chennāgi baralla, iṅgliṣ baruttā?
phrases.en: I don't speak Kannada well, do you speak English?

grammar.title: 'If ... then': the conditional -ಅರೆ
grammar.body:
Add **-ಅರೆ** *-are* (spoken **-್ರೆ** *-re*, e.g. ಮಾಡಿದ್ರೆ) to the **past stem** of the verb. It has no personal endings:
ಮಾಡು → ಮಾಡಿದರೆ / ಮಾಡಿದ್ರೆ 'if (I/you/they) do'
ಬರು → ಬಂದರೆ / ಬಂದ್ರೆ 'if ... come'
ಹೋಗು → ಹೋದರೆ / ಹೋದ್ರೆ 'if ... go'
ಇರು → ಇದ್ದರೆ / ಇದ್ರೆ 'if ... is / there is'
ಆಗು → ಆದರೆ / ಆದ್ರೆ 'if it happens / if it's possible' (also the word 'but')
ಬೇಕು → ಬೇಕಾದರೆ 'if (you) want'

The 'if' clause comes first; the 'then' clause follows with no word for 'then' (sometimes ಆಗ 'then'): ಮಳೆ ಬಂದರೆ ನಾನು ಬರಲ್ಲ 'if it rains, I won't come'.

**Negative 'if not'** = infinitive stem + **-ಅದಿದ್ದರೆ** (spoken -ಅದಿದ್ರೆ / -ಅಲ್ಲಾಂದ್ರೆ): ಬರದಿದ್ದರೆ 'if (you) don't come', ಸಿಗದಿದ್ದರೆ 'if (it) isn't found'.

**Unreal past** ('if I had ..., I would have ...') = -ಇದ್ದರೆ + past habitual: ಗೊತ್ತಿದ್ದರೆ ಹೇಳ್ತಿದ್ದೆ 'if I had known, I would have told you'.

examples.native: ಏನಾದ್ರೂ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ ಆದ್ರೆ ನನಗೆ ಫೋನ್ ಮಾಡಿ
examples.roman: ēnādrū samasye ādre nanage phōn māḍi
examples.en: If there's any problem, call me.
If you leave early, you'll catch the train.
If the passport isn't found, file a complaint with the police.
If you're not well, go to a doctor.
If I'd known, I would have told you.

grammar.title: 'Even if' -ಅರೂ, and 'when' -ಆಗ
grammar.body:
Two close relatives of the conditional:

**Even if / although** = past stem + **-ಅರೂ** (conditional + -ಊ 'even'): ಮಳೆ ಬಂದರೂ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll come even if it rains', ಎಷ್ಟು ಹುಡುಕಿದರೂ ಸಿಗಲಿಲ್ಲ 'however much I searched, I didn't find it'. With question words it means '-ever': ಏನಾದರೂ 'anything (whatever happens)', ಯಾರಾದರೂ 'anyone', ಎಲ್ಲಾದರೂ 'anywhere' (spoken ಏನಾದ್ರೂ, ಯಾರಾದ್ರೂ, ಎಲ್ಲಾದ್ರೂ).

**When** = relative participle (past -ಇದ / present -ಉವ) + **-ಆಗ**: ಬಂದಾಗ 'when (someone) came / comes', ಹೋಗುವಾಗ 'while going', ಚಿಕ್ಕವನಿದ್ದಾಗ 'when I was small'. Spoken ಹೋಗುವಾಗ → ಹೋಗೋವಾಗ / ಹೋಗ್ತಾ ಇರುವಾಗ.

examples.en: However much I searched, I couldn't find my bag.

examples.native: ನಾನು ರೈಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮಲಗಿದ್ದಾಗ ಕಳ್ಳ ಫೋನ್ ಕದ್ದ
examples.roman: nānu railinalli malagiddāga kaḷḷa phōn kadda
examples.en: While I was asleep on the train, a thief stole my phone.
Call when you reach the hotel.
It doesn't matter even if you're late, come safely.

dialogue.title: At the police station
dialogue.setting: Ben's phone was stolen on a crowded bus; he goes to a police station in Shivajinagar.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ ಸಾರ್. ನನ್ನ ಫೋನ್ ಕಳ್ಳತನ ಆಗಿದೆ. ದೂರು ಕೊಡಬೇಕು.
lines.roman: namaskāra sār. nanna phōn kaḷḷatana āgide. dūru koḍabēku.
lines.en: Hello sir. My phone has been stolen. I need to make a complaint.

lines.speaker: Police
lines.en: Sit down. Where and when did it happen?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: ಇವತ್ತು ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಬಸ್ಸಲ್ಲಿ. ತುಂಬಾ ಜನ ಇದ್ರು. ಇಳಿದಾಗ ಫೋನ್ ಇರಲಿಲ್ಲ.
lines.roman: ivattu beḷigge bassalli. tumbā jana idru. iḷidāga phōn iralilla.
lines.en: This morning on the bus. It was very crowded. When I got off, the phone wasn't there.

lines.speaker: Police
lines.native: ಯಾವ ಬಸ್ಸು? ಫೋನ್ ಯಾವ ಕಂಪನಿ, ಯಾವ ಬಣ್ಣ?
lines.roman: yāva bassu? phōn yāva kampani, yāva baṇṇa?
lines.en: Which bus? What make and colour is the phone?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: ಮುನ್ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತೈದು ಇ. ಕಪ್ಪು ಬಣ್ಣದ ಸ್ಯಾಮ್ಸಂಗ್.
lines.roman: munnūra mūvattaidu i. kappu baṇṇada syāmsaṅg.

lines.speaker: Police
lines.native: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಗುರುತಿನ ಚೀಟಿ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಳಾಸ ಕೊಡಿ.
lines.roman: nimma gurutina chīṭi mattu viḷāsa koḍi.
lines.en: Give me your ID and address.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: ಇದು ನನ್ನ ಪಾಸ್ಪೋರ್ಟ್. ಫೋನ್ ಸಿಕ್ಕಿದರೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತಾಗುತ್ತೆ?
lines.roman: idu nanna pāspōrṭ. phōn sikkidare hēge gottāgutte?
lines.en: Here's my passport. If the phone is found, how will I know?

lines.speaker: Police
lines.native: ಸಿಕ್ಕಿದರೆ ನಾವೇ ಫೋನ್ ಮಾಡ್ತೀವಿ. ಈ ನಂಬರಿಗೆ ಕರೀರಿ, ಏನಾದ್ರೂ ಬೇಕಾದ್ರೆ.
lines.roman: sikkidare nāvē phōn māḍtīvi. ī nambarige karīri, ēnādrū bēkādre.
lines.en: If it's found, we'll call you ourselves. Call this number if you need anything.

culture: India's single emergency number is **112**; 100 (police), 101 (fire) and 108 (ambulance) also still work in Karnataka. In a crisis, bystanders are usually quick to help: calling out ಅಣ್ಣ or ಅಕ್ಕ will get attention. Keep a photocopy of your passport and visa, as hotels must register foreign guests. When travelling by KSRTC bus or train, people commonly say ಶುಭ ಪ್ರಯಾಣ 'have a good journey' or, less formally, ಹುಷಾರಾಗಿ ಹೋಗಿ ಬನ್ನಿ 'go safely and come back'.
